title: Noise robustness for cross-field singularity detection (PATCH-39 follow-up)
description:
**Surfaced during PATCH-39.** Per-edge rounding in the simplified BZK12 solver produces spurious singularities on triangulation-noisy meshes. Procedural.obj (24k faces, χ=8) produced 5788 singularities; expected ~hundreds. Clean meshes (cube, sphere, torus) work correctly.

Fixes per Campen 2014 thesis Sec 4.4:
- Use scale-aware field energy [RVAL09, ECBK14] to suppress small-scale curvature noise.
- Or apply Laplacian smoothing to the angle-defect input before the LSQ.
- Or add a persistence threshold — discard singularity pairs whose index sum is small and whose physical separation is below ε.
- Or implement the FULL BZK12 greedy round-and-resolve loop (PATCH-39 used a 3-stage simplified pipeline). Greedy rounding orders integer commits by confidence and re-solves, dramatically reducing spurious singularities on noisy inputs.

The simplified pipeline is provably equivalent on smooth closed manifolds. The full BZK12 should fix noisy meshes.
definition-of-done: 1. Procedural.obj produces ≤200 singularities (down from 5788). 2. Sum(index4) still equals 4χ. 3. Clean meshes (cube/sphere/torus) unchanged. 4. Document which fix was implemented (greedy BZK12, persistence filter, or scale-aware energy).
testing-plan: 1. Procedural.obj count + sum check. 2. Clean-mesh regression: cube/sphere/torus tests still pass. 3. Hand.obj baseline comparison: count within 20% of metriko's stage1_singular.txt.
